name: Table
purpose: Compare records across the same few columns.
description: Compact rows with subtle filled backgrounds. Injected cells render as text.

guidance.summary: Shows records in rows and their attributes in columns, so people can scan, compare, and sort exact values.
useWhen: People compare the same few attributes across many records, such as traffic sources and their visitors.
Values must be read exactly, not estimated from a shape.
People look for a particular record among many; make the table sortable past six rows.

avoidWhen.text: The point is a trend over time, not exact values.
The point is how a whole splits into parts.
Two or three options are compared on the same measures to pick one.
People need to search, filter, select, edit, or page through many records.

states.label: Default
states.description: Rows in the order given, under column headers.

states.label: Sortable
states.description: Column headers become buttons with a sort mark.

states.label: Sorted
states.description: Pressing a header sorts by it: figures largest first, text A to Z. A second press reverses the order, and a third restores the original.

dos.text: Give every table a caption that says what its rows are.
dos.why: Screen reader users hear the caption first; it is how they know what the table is about.

dos.text: Put units in the column header and keep each cell to its value.
dos.why: Short cells line up and can be compared at a glance.

dos.text: Make the table sortable once it has more than six rows.
dos.why: Past a screenful, people look for the largest value or a particular record rather than reading in order.

dos.text: When it is not sortable, order rows by what matters most, such as the largest value first.
dos.why: The first rows get most of the attention.

donts.text: Don’t use a table to lay out a page.
donts.why: Screen readers announce rows and columns that are not data.

donts.text: Don’t put sentences or paragraphs in cells.
donts.why: Rows grow uneven and the columns stop being scannable; put the detail in a region or a detail view.

donts.text: Don’t use colour alone to say a value is good or bad.
donts.why: Write the sign or a word too, such as +24% or Down 6%.

donts.text: Don’t add a column that is the same in every row.
donts.why: It costs width and attention and says nothing; say it once in the caption.

content: Column headers are short nouns: Source, People, Change.
Write a column’s numbers the same way all the way down: the same decimals and the same unit.

notes: Headers are th elements with scope="col", so every cell is read with its column.
The caption names the table; it may be visually hidden, but it must be there.
A sorted column sets aria-sort, so the order is announced.

rows.description: One array of cell strings per row, one cell for each column. Columns of figures align on the right.

sortable.description: Let people sort by any column: figures largest first, text A to Z.
